Caveman 4.0.1 source archive: BENIGN
====================================

Sample: 717ad5815e7c8958614f91934af20a455c9dc57265be23585c13562936513f94
Identity: JuliusBrussee/caveman, root package caveman-installer 4.0.1.
Purpose: agent prose/input compression, local agent hooks and provider proxy.

The earlier v4.0.0 release was fetched with forager into scratch/version-drift/
prior. Its original archive SHA-256 is:
d7aa04c47624af3f98ed7ef3de5d0bb3b1aa3b528a780233485a5bd0e5b03f94
URL: https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/archive/refs/tags/v4.0.0.tar.gz
The tarball and .forage.json are retained alongside the extracted original.

Decisive diff evidence
----------------------
The full tree diff contains 176 changed files. src/hooks/install.sh,
src/hooks/caveman-activate.js, the middleware LiteLLM adapter, and its
contracts test are byte-identical in v4.0.0. installer/install.js changes
only its pinned download ref from v4.0.0 to v4.0.1. Current rules also flag
the earlier release, so the supplied clean-to-alert history does not establish
new behavior in these files.

Reviewed runtime changes implement Codex result unwrapping, conservative
compression/repair checks, atomic model-override writes, Windows command
quoting/window handling, Pi provider/recovery compatibility and local Pi
session analysis, SQLite deadlines, configured credential/header forwarding,
and batching of the existing explicit account sync. CI changes update agent
pins, Python release hashes and permissions. No new concealed execution or
unrelated data recipient was identified in the reviewed diff.

Execution paths and false claims
--------------------------------
1. src/hooks/install.sh preflights settings, copies local hook files or uses
   curl to acquire them, chmods the statusline, backs up settings, and writes
   local node commands into SessionStart/SubagentStart/UserPromptSubmit/
   SessionEnd registrations. It does not put curl in the session command.
   caveman-activate.js reads local mode/config/skill files, updates local mode
   state, applies local agent model overrides and emits hookSpecificOutput.
   Its imported config/override helpers supply no network beacon. Installation
   traffic beside a SessionStart name cannot establish recurring network C2.

2. installer/install.js uses private temporary directories for release-pinned
   hook downloads. The remote branch verifies every hook against SHA-256
   checksums before staging/renaming into the hook directory. Its process calls
   perform curl fallback, agent CLI registration and local probes. runInit
   runs only the shipped local caveman-init.js; it explicitly refuses the
   former unsigned remote download-and-execute fallback. A download, /tmp
   reference and unrelated process call do not bind the downloaded file to
   an execution sink.

3. caveman_middleware/litellm.py imports native LiteLLM and CustomLogger,
   registers a removable instance-scoped callback and projects compression
   through native SDK/router calls. litellm_params/litellm_call_id identify
   request metadata and call accounting in that adapter and its tests, not
   a relocated library implementation. Ordinary callback vocabulary cannot
   establish a clone-and-rename distribution.

4. caveman-compress takes an explicit filepath, resolves it, rejects secret-
   like names before reading, and checks size and prose type. It masks code,
   calls the configured CLI/Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible provider, validates
   output and stages the result with an out-of-tree backup. Repair requests
   can send the original file. This is real, disclosed file-content transfer
   for the requested compression operation, not unauthorized exfiltration.
   The new SKILL text explains that boundary; the filename denylist already
   existed in v4.0.0. Endpoint settings and user data sensitivity are deployment
   context not available from this artifact.

Readable source was traced through callers, callbacks and write/launch sinks;
archive and member cleave facts (including decoded strings) were captured in
scratch. The reviewed paths do not rely on a concealed encoded payload. The
source's byte-oriented compression, hashes and encoded protocol data implement
its stated functionality. The verdict is based on these paths and the diff,
not on classifier scores or the absence of other alerts.

Rule changes and preservation
------------------------------
- Replace the false hostile session-beacon claim with a notable IPC hook
  observation requiring an actual curl/wget command field and SessionStart
  configuration syntax. It reports co-occurrence, not an inferred send chain.
  The command-field atom lives with source key/value syntax. All original
  network and local-hook primitives remain available.
- Replace generic download/process co-occurrence with a notable file-exec
  deployment pattern binding HTTP response -> writer -> finish callback ->
  launch of the same destination identifier. Require the same writer/response
  handles and an argument-free finish callback (no shadowed target parameter).
  Retain temporary-path and DNS/chmod context as neutral qualified observations;
  update the obfuscated-DNS consumer to use the linked chain. Plain downloads,
  temp paths, chmod and program launches remain independently detected.
- Move the call-id/provider key matchers unchanged into metadata source setting
  vocabulary. Require an internal completion-pipeline function definition plus
  field evidence before calling a source file LiteLLM implementation. Update
  both identity composites and inspect exact/ancestor consumers.

Controls and final scans
-------------------------
python3 testdata/triage/caveman-version-drift/check.py passes eight cases from
neutral temporary paths: linked stream launch, DNS context, different executable,
different writer, shadowed target, network command field, install-only curl and
independent LiteLLM adapter. The fixtures also have expectations.toml entries.

Before/after scans of existing hidden-downloaded-file.js and
mastra-setup-dropper.cjs retain their supported attack findings. No supported
attack finding disappears from those controls. Genuine implementation source
from Hanzo 1.82.2 and upstream LiteLLM 1.106.2 retains identity recognition;
Hanzo's current README/NOTICE disclose its fork, so this is source-identity
preservation, not a malicious-verdict claim. The older Hanzo 1.81.15 already
renamed away the old field fingerprint and is not lost coverage.

The isolated repository baseline and edited atomscan runs use explicit trait
directories and --follow=none; all 1,719 emitted entries have matching hashes.
Baseline: two distinct suspicious claims (five aggregate/member occurrences).
Edited: zero hostile or suspicious findings. The initial installed default
pack also reproduced the reported hostile hook finding; its rules differ from
the repository baseline. The full following scan after correction also has
zero hostile/suspicious findings, including the fetched GitHub self-reference.
The calibrated classifier remains benign (level -1) before and after, despite
raw probability rising from 0.58625966 to 0.6582347 in the isolated comparison.
No classifier miss is exposed, and no trait was added to manipulate the score.

comparison.json records all lost and gained IDs. Besides the corrected
inferences/identity labels and moved field tokens, 25 low-tier temp-tmp grouping
findings stop being emitted after their broad parent is removed. Both constituent
/tmp observations remain in every affected file with unchanged matchers; this
loses no path evidence. No other isolated scan finding is lost. consumer-audit.json
records exact references and ancestor-selector counts. Full raw scans, facts,
source diff, controls and acquisition provenance remain in scratch/version-drift.

Validation also exposed the older compact-js-fetch-chmod-exec objective on the
new ordinary download/chmod control. Its matcher combined independent network,
chmod and execution calls and had no attack admission. Its only two consumers
are js-platform-native-download-execute and compact-js-fetch-chmod-exec-cleanup;
there are no exact positive fixture expectations for that base rule. Replace
that base with a neutral file-exec capability requiring a linked HTTP writer/
finish/launch or the existing destination-bound download-helper/spawn pattern,
plus HTTP-to-file and chmod context. Update both consumers. The unconsumed
compact-js-download-call group is removed; all three constituent HTTP/helper
observations remain canonical. Existing malicious-fixture attack coverage is
compared again after this correction. The new DNS control permits no suspicious
or hostile findings in the final expectations.

Final required check: make validate (run after this record and marker are written).
